DEC-DOCUMENT-EVIDENCE-QUALITYAppliedDocument evidence and quality2026-09-07

Make document quality review evidence-backed

Use the Site for reusable methods and a source-grounded brief for each application. Treat integrity, chronology, and extraction as prerequisites to judging reader and document quality.

DecisionExpand the existing editorial skills, reconcile Leah and Sofia, use a small content trial, and require version-specific independent findings before a review can pass.
EvidenceA resume audit found changed attribution and action verbs, weakened context, cosmetic variations, and approval labels without inspectable review evidence. The process is adopted; its effect on the next resume remains untested.
AlternativesAnother full visual redesign; a universal resume score; additional personas; an app-managed runtime. Start with existing capabilities and a bounded trial.
TradeoffsClaim tracking and concrete findings take more care. Focus them on consequential claims and affected checks; do not add a general approval ritual to every edit.
AffectsSkills, Leah, Sofia, job-search handoffs, and Docs. Trial procedure remains isolated.
Revisit whenA real trial still produces generic or misleading content, the reviewer cannot find evidence, or the process creates effort without improving the reader’s understanding.
DEC-001AppliedInformation architecture2026-09-04

Flow hierarchy for persona work

Organize each person’s work into foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows, with the activity inventory embedded inside each flow.

QuestionShould the persona page follow a day, a list of activities, or the outcomes the person is trying to produce?
DecisionUse flow hierarchy as the primary structure. Each tier can contain multiple workflows.
RationaleThis keeps cadence, tools, priorities, friction, and recovery work attached to the context where they matter.
AffectsPersona cards, persona detail views, and the persona-research guidance.
EvidenceLayout Lab prototype · Current Docs guidance
Revisit whenReal persona research shows that users need a different first-order way to compare work.
DEC-002AppliedSkill presentation2026-09-04

Skill index plus deep dive

Keep the complete capability set visible, then select one skill to inspect its triggers, operating model, quality signals, workflows, and evidence.

QuestionCan someone see all the capabilities and still understand one skill deeply?
DecisionUse a scan-friendly skill index with a focused deep-dive panel.
RationaleThe index supports orientation; depth belongs in the selected skill instead of a wall of content.
AffectsPersona detail pages, the Skills space, and the $persona-skills guidance.
EvidenceSkill Layout Lab prototype · Current Docs guidance
Revisit whenSkill reuse or relationship density makes the index difficult to scan or the panel too shallow.

DEC-007AppliedInformation architecture2026-09-10

Operating Packs are contextual library space

Catalog reusable, file-based operating context alongside the existing library spaces while keeping actual Markdown source outside the catalog when appropriate.

QuestionWhere should domain or project instructions, standards, conventions, procedures, references, and validation guidance live when they are reusable but not executable capabilities?
DecisionAdd Operating Packs as a first-class space with a small source/location record, explicit availability, and scoped Persona, Skill, workflow, Playbook, and Tool-use relationships.
RationaleContextual rules need a durable home that does not turn Skills into project instruction or Playbooks into duplicated policy. Scoped applications keep a pack relevant to the work where it applies.
TradeoffsThe catalog does not transport or execute packs, and external references may remain planned or unavailable until verified. Project conventions remain local unless later evidence supports broader reuse.
AffectsOrientation routing, Docs, Site navigation, the Operating Pack catalog, lifecycle Skills, and reconciliation guidance. Existing Persona, Skill, Tool, and Playbook definitions remain separate.
Revisit whenA pack needs executable runtime behavior, repeated rules reveal a generalizable Skill, a Playbook duplicates pack content, or external source transport becomes a separately authorized product need.
DEC-008AppliedInformation architecture2026-09-11

Templates are reusable starting artifacts

Add Templates as a first-class library space beside Operating Packs while preserving a distinct ownership boundary for reusable starting structure.

QuestionWhere should reusable starting structures and scaffolds live when they accelerate work but do not define how the work should be performed?
DecisionCatalog Template identity, purpose, applicability, source metadata, evidence, lifecycle, revision context, and relationships in Persona-Library. Keep actual reusable artifacts in their canonical external or project source.
RationaleTemplates answer what to start from. Operating Packs answer how to work within context; Skills own reusable judgment; Tools own execution and permissions; Playbooks own coordination and outcomes. A scoped Persona–Skill–workflow application keeps applicability contextual.
TradeoffsThe static catalog can describe a planned external artifact without making it available. The system does not fetch, clone, render, execute, publish, or upgrade Template artifacts yet; project-specific starters remain local until evidence supports promotion.
AffectsOrientation routing, Template source/model normalization, lifecycle Skills, validation, Docs, Site navigation, generated data, and reconciliation guidance. The three initial design-system identities remain planned because the inspected external repository contains only README.md.
EvidenceTemplates catalog · Docs boundary · inspected rickvang/template-library main revision f88a4011902b58b2f192305f5a731f1a71263965
Revisit whenExternal Template paths become real, a project starter demonstrates broader reuse, Template relationships need new dimensions, or artifact transport/execution becomes a separately authorized Tool or workflow capability.
DEC-009AppliedPersona boundary2026-09-11

Template Librarian stewards the collection

Add a library-stewardship Persona for Template discoverability, provenance, lifecycle, and routing while keeping substantive Template quality with domain specialists.

QuestionWho keeps the Template collection organized and trustworthy without becoming the domain expert for every artifact?
DecisionUse the Template Librarian to maintain catalog identity, source verification, duplication control, promotion, deprecation, relocation, and reconciliation. Route discipline-specific research and composition to the relevant specialist.
RationaleLibrary stewardship and domain judgment are different kinds of work. Keeping them separate preserves the Template boundary and lets the collection grow without turning one Persona into a polymath.
AffectsTemplate routing, Persona workflows and handoffs, Template lifecycle Skills, Docs, generated Persona output, and reconciliation. Mara Okoye remains the escalation point for architecture, taxonomy, and concept-boundary questions.
EvidenceTemplate Librarian Persona · Templates catalog · Templates guidance · Issue #63
Revisit whenObserved Template work shows that stewardship and domain composition cannot remain separate, a dedicated reusable capability is justified, or the external artifact ownership boundary changes.
DEC-010AppliedPlaybook boundary2026-09-14

Bounded parallel implementation is a distinct Playbook

Keep Multi-Persona Collaboration as named-Persona synthesis through a shared problem-context. Catalog bounded parallel repository implementation as its own Playbook with Coordinator, Implementer, Reviewer, and Authorizer roles.

QuestionShould usage-conscious parallel implementation be a new Playbook or a profile of Multi-Persona Collaboration, especially while #71 is still open?
DecisionAdd playbook-bounded-parallel-implementation as a distinct Playbook. Reference collaboration instead of copying its stages, solution-quality gate, or problem-context contract. Do not create an Agent, Coordinator, Runtime, Budget, or Scheduler entity.
RationaleCollaboration produces one inspectable solution from Persona lenses. Bounded parallel implementation produces independent reviewable PRs with one-level delegation, compact GitHub-reference handoffs, independent review, and separately authorized merge. Those outcomes and gates are materially different.
AlternativesExtend Multi-Persona Collaboration with an implementation profile; wait for #71 before adding identity; encode ChatGPT Work or Codex as canonical meaning. Rejected because they mix synthesis with mutation gates or bind the contract to a runtime.
AffectsPlaybook catalog, Playbooks orientation route, Site Playbooks and Docs surfaces, root AGENTS.md activation, and Work Order evidence for issue #82. Collaboration methodology is unchanged.
Revisit when#71 catalogs collaboration identity, a two-repository proof is needed, or runtime-specific procedure becomes substantial enough for a Tool package.

DEC-011AppliedRole boundary2026-09-14

Riley orchestrates job search; the Playbook owns the outcome

Keep Riley Morgan’s identity as AI orchestrator. Make the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook the front door for the full outcome. Specialists own domain judgment. Do not create a generic Job Search Persona or store private job history in Persona-Library.

QuestionShould Riley Morgan become the domain-owning Job Search Persona, or remain a reusable orchestrator for the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook?
DecisionPlaybook owns the outcome. Riley Morgan · AI orchestrator coordinates contributors. Elena, Marcus, Leah, Samira, Camille, and Sofia retain specialist ownership. Private opportunity history uses the job ledger contract in candidate workspace state. No new Job Search Persona.
RationaleCollapsing job-search expertise into Riley would make the reusable AI orchestrator identity accumulate domain methods and blur specialist quality criteria. Playbook-first wording preserves reusable orchestration across domains while keeping search strategy, hiring calibration, narrative, outreach, visual, and document judgment with the existing specialists.
AlternativesCreate a new Job Search Persona; rename Riley to Job Search Orchestrator; leave “job-search orchestrator” labels as-is. Rejected because no uncovered responsibility justified a new Persona, and identity drift would damage reuse.
AffectsJob-search implementation guidance, Playbooks and job-search Site surfaces, Docs orientation route resume-application-work, Elena’s search workflow/skill wording, job ledger contract, and Work Order evidence for issue #90. Riley’s canonical roleLabel remains AI orchestrator.
Revisit whenImplementation evidence shows a real uncovered job-search responsibility not owned by Elena, Marcus, Leah, Samira, Camille, Sofia, Riley, or the Playbook; or when a callable job-search Skill package is authorized beyond the ledger contract.
Status noteThe front-door conclusion is qualified by DEC-013; the actor-like Playbook outcome-ownership conclusion is further qualified by DEC-014. The remaining Riley identity, specialist ownership, and privacy boundaries remain applied.
DEC-012AppliedPlaybook boundary2026-09-14

Template lifecycle is a distinct Playbook

Catalog playbook-template-lifecycle as the reusable coordination model for researching, composing, promoting, maintaining, and reconciling Templates. Keep Elena Park as steward, domain specialists as quality owners, Mara as architecture escalation, and Template Skills as stage procedures.

QuestionShould the Template lifecycle remain only a sequence of Skills and Librarian workflows, or become a canonical Playbook?
DecisionAdd playbook-template-lifecycle / Research, promote, and maintain a reusable Template. Reference existing Template Librarian workflows, Template Skills, domain specialists, DEC-008/009, and external template-library ownership instead of copying them. Do not create a new Persona, Skill, registry, or runtime.
RationaleThe Template system already crosses stewardship, domain quality, external artifact ownership, promotion evidence, and reconciliation. That repeated cross-owner outcome needs an inspectable stage/gate contract without turning every bounded Template Skill action into a mandatory Playbook run.
AlternativesLeave the outcome undocumented; fold it into Skill formation; invent a Template runtime/registry. Rejected because the owners and gates are already Template-specific and distinct from skill formation or execution infrastructure.
AffectsPlaybook catalog, Playbooks orientation route, Templates stewardship handoff, Site Playbooks/Docs/Decisions surfaces, and Work Order evidence for issue #72. Template Skills and Librarian identity remain unchanged. Numbered DEC-012 after DEC-011 on the Riley/job-search ownership boundary.

DEC-013AppliedRouting boundary2026-09-15

Riley is the default routing front door

Riley Morgan is the default interaction and routing front door for unqualified requests while Playbooks retain procedural ownership and specialists retain domain judgment.

QuestionHow should an unqualified request enter the Persona Library when the work may be narrow specialist work or a larger reusable outcome?
DecisionRiley interprets intent and selects the smallest useful route: narrow work may go to a specialist or Skill; outcome-scale work may go to a Playbook; a bounded consultation, Tool path, or other focused route may be selected when that is the smallest useful fit. Explicit requests naming a specialist, Skill, or Playbook may route directly without an artificial Riley hop.
RationaleIssue #90 correctly removed job-search domain ownership from Riley, but its front-door wording also made the Evidence-led Job Search Playbook appear to be the default entry. Separating entry/routing ownership from procedural and domain ownership restores the intended interaction model without adding a runtime router or moving expertise.
AlternativesKeep the Playbook as the universal front door; make Riley own the complete job-search method; add a routing service or registry. Rejected because these options either force taxonomy-first interaction, transfer specialist judgment, or add unnecessary runtime architecture.
TradeoffsRiley must choose among routes without absorbing their expertise. The route contract needs explicit tests and should be revisited if observed requests consistently choose a larger or less capable path than the smallest useful route.
Affectsdocs/job-search/implementation.md; content/orientation/docs.json; Riley’s authored record and maintenance history; routing validators/tests; generated library and Decisions output; issue #111.
EvidenceIssue #111, PR #112, the Riley Persona/workflow sources, the four explicit routing tests, and Mara’s placement review recorded in the issue-111 Work Order.
QualifiesDEC-011
Revisit whenObserved requests show that Riley’s route selection consistently chooses a larger or less capable path than the smallest useful route, or a later Decision establishes a different universal entry contract.
DEC-014AppliedPersona / Playbook boundary2026-09-16

Personas operate Playbooks; job search gets a domain orchestrator

Keep Riley Morgan as the default routing front door for unqualified requests, then use Priya Desai · Job search orchestrator as the operating Persona for full-outcome Evidence-led Job Search. Treat Playbooks as process surfaces rather than autonomous actors.

QuestionAfter Riley routes an unqualified request, who exercises judgment and remains responsible for a full Playbook run when the Playbook itself is a process surface rather than an actor?
DecisionRiley remains the default system entry and routing point for unqualified requests. A Persona operates a Playbook. For full-outcome job search, Riley routes to job-search-orchestrator / Priya Desai; Priya operates playbook-evidence-led-job-search. The Playbook defines stages, shared state, handoffs, quality gates, recovery, and learning but does not independently exercise judgment or own the outcome. Explicit requests for Priya, a specialist, a Skill, or the Playbook may route directly.
RationaleDEC-013 restored Riley as the default routing front door. Issue #113 addresses a separate layer: DEC-011 also gave the Playbook actor-like outcome ownership. A dedicated domain orchestrator fills that operating role without transferring specialist expertise into Riley or into the Playbook.
AlternativesKeep the Playbook as actor/owner; make Riley the job-search domain operator; stretch Elena into end-to-end orchestration. Rejected because each option blurs an existing responsibility boundary.
TradeoffsThe architecture gains one additional Persona and routing hop for unqualified full-outcome job-search work. In return, entry/routing, process operation, process structure, and specialist judgment remain explicit and independently testable.
AffectsArchitecture; Playbook composition guidance; Riley/Priya job-search routing; Evidence-led Job Search docs and Site surfaces; Docs orientation; job ledger orchestration wording; application Work Order fields; generated validation; issue #113.
EvidenceIssue #113, PR #114, canonical Priya Persona/workflows/Skill applications, the Riley-first routing contract from DEC-013, and focused validation.
QualifiesDEC-011
Revisit whenReal job-search runs show Priya is redundant with Riley or Elena, Persona-operated Playbooks reduce clarity or completeness, or a later Decision establishes a different durable operator boundary.
DEC-015AppliedCandidate application source boundary2026-09-18

A designated candidate baseline preserves the career spine

When current standing decisions designate a private master or baseline resume, resolve it before role tailoring. Reusable Templates and normalized resume models remain separate layers and must not silently reconstruct the candidate's approved career spine.

QuestionHow should reusable Templates and normalized resume content interact with an explicitly promoted private candidate master?
DecisionAdd Candidate Baseline Resume as a private Candidate Context layer. Standing decisions determine whether one is active. Resolve the exact baseline source and revision before resume composition, use it as the default composition baseline for the protected career spine, keep evidence authoritative for factual truth, keep reusable Templates authoritative only for reusable presentation structure, and use normalized resume content as an optional portability layer. Material protected-field changes require a verified evidence correction or explicit candidate decision; intentional material omissions are recorded as omitted_with_reason; an unresolved designated baseline blocks the affected resume composition.
RationaleThe 2026-09-18 Tessera Labs packet bypassed the candidate's active standing decisions and Google Docs master, then reconstructed the resume from stale or secondary context. That run dropped recent employers, changed chronology and contact data, weakened quantified evidence, and produced a materially different ATS artifact. The September 16–17 Candidate Context, Resume Content Model, and semantic Template mapping work separated reusable structure from candidate data correctly but left the promoted private baseline implicit rather than first-class.
AlternativesRemove the reusable Template and Resume Content Model architecture; promote the private master into the reusable Template library; or always regenerate role resumes from evidence/model data. Rejected because the first loses useful reusable infrastructure, the second leaks candidate-specific composition into a reusable artifact boundary, and the third repeats the failure mode this decision is intended to prevent.
TradeoffsApplication runs gain one explicit private-source resolution step and one baseline-to-output integrity comparison. That adds a small amount of process state, but it prevents silent loss of approved candidate chronology and structure while preserving the ability to use materially different verified Templates when needed.
Affectsdocs/job-search/implementation.md; docs/job-search/candidate-context-contract.md; docs/job-search/candidate-context-integration.md; docs/job-search/resume-template-mapping.md; docs/job-search/application-work-order-template.md; .agents/skills/resume-template-semantic-mapping/SKILL.md; content/orientation/docs.json and generated route data; validation guards/tests; Candidate Application Context Operating Pack; issue #148.
EvidenceIssue #148; Rick Vang — Resume Standing Decisions; Rick Vang Resume — Master Template; evidence-led prior application records; the failed Tessera Labs packet comparison; Persona-Library semantic mapping merge #123; operating-packs normalized resume context merge #4.
QualifiesDEC-008
Revisit whenA future candidate explicitly replaces the baseline with a different source-of-truth model, repeated runs show baseline drift creates more conflicts than it prevents, or a validated normalized candidate model becomes the explicitly designated composition baseline through a later candidate decision.
DEC-016SupersededPrivate application tracking boundary2026-09-18

Application tracking stays private and extractable

Add a top-level Applications surface while keeping real opportunity and application records browser-local, portable, and independent of canonical Persona and Skill data.

QuestionHow can Persona Library support application tracking now without publishing private job history or making a later standalone app difficult to extract?
DecisionShip application tracking as a separate top-level Applications companion surface. Persona Library owns the tracker code, portable record schema, lifecycle vocabulary, and export/import behavior; real application records remain browser-local private state and never become canonical repository data. Keep seen-job deduplication, candidate context, and application lifecycle tracking as separate contracts.
RationaleThe requester wants application tracking inside Persona Library now but may make Persona Library public later or split the tracker into its own app. Coupling records to Persona/Skill data or committing opportunity history would create a privacy problem and an expensive extraction boundary. Browser-local persistence provides useful single-user state while versioned JSON keeps the data portable.
AlternativesStore application records in Git; overload the seen-job deduplication contract; embed lifecycle state directly into the job-search Playbook page; or build a separate app immediately. Rejected because they respectively expose private history, collapse distinct state models, couple persistence to orchestration presentation, or add infrastructure before it is needed.
TradeoffsBrowser-local storage is single-device and can be lost when browser data is cleared, so export is the backup and migration path. In return, the repository stays publishable, the MVP needs no backend or authentication, and a future standalone app can replace only the storage adapter rather than untangling canonical library records.
AffectsTop-level Applications Site surface; build/navigation; docs/job-search/application-tracker-contract.md; job-search implementation and candidate-context boundaries; architecture; generated validation; issue #151.
EvidenceRequester decision on 2026-09-18; public Persona-Library repository boundary; existing private candidate-context and seen-job contracts; issue #151; WO-2026-09-18-job-application-tracker.
Status noteSuperseded by DEC-017 after application tracking required authenticated cross-device and agent-accessible persistence. DEC-016 remains the historical MVP boundary.
QualifiesDEC-011, DEC-014
Revisit whenApplication tracking needs authenticated cross-device sync, collaboration, external integrations, or server-side automation; browser-local recovery proves insufficient; or extraction into a standalone app begins.
DEC-017AppliedPrivate application tracking boundary2026-09-19

Authenticated storage becomes primary for private application tracking

Keep Persona-Library as the code and contract owner while moving real opportunity rows behind an authenticated Supabase storage adapter; preserve Git as canonical authoring for library catalogs.

QuestionWhere should private application state live now that browser-local persistence prevents reliable cross-device and authorized agent updates, and should the same database become the canonical home for Persona-Library catalogs?
DecisionUse authenticated Supabase storage as the primary opportunity store when configured. Persona-Library owns the tracker UI, portable schema, storage adapter, database contract, and migration/export behavior, but real opportunity rows remain private operational data outside Git. Keep browser-local state only as an explicit fallback, migration source, and rollback copy; never silently redirect a failed remote write to local storage. Keep Personas, Skills, Tools, Templates, Operating Packs, Playbooks, Docs, Decisions, and Work Orders canonical in Git. Any later Supabase catalog tables are deterministic read-only projections from those authored sources, not a replacement authoring system.
RationaleThe local-only MVP protected privacy and extraction, but it prevents ChatGPT/Codex workflows from reliably creating or updating tracked opportunities and does not provide cross-device persistence. A storage adapter preserves the extraction boundary while authenticated RLS-backed storage solves the operational requirement. Keeping catalog authoring in Git retains reviewable diffs, provenance, validation, and deterministic builds while still allowing a future query index.
AlternativesKeep localStorage and rely on import/handoff files; store opportunity history in Git; repurpose an unrelated existing Supabase project; move all canonical catalogs into database tables; or split Applications into a separate app immediately. These respectively preserve the integration constraint, violate privacy, blur project ownership, weaken Git-based authoring/provenance, or add extraction work before the storage boundary is proven.
TradeoffsThe tracker now depends on authentication, deployment configuration, RLS, and an external service when remote mode is enabled. Local fallback/export remains important for recovery. Catalog projection adds synchronization responsibility later, so it is deferred until opportunity persistence is proven.
AffectsApplications storage/runtime, build configuration, docs/job-search/application-tracker-contract.md, architecture, validation, issue #156, future catalog projection, and the later disposition of issue #153.
EvidenceRequester direction on 2026-09-19; issue #156; current browser-local integration constraint; current Supabase documentation for publishable browser clients, custom Data API schemas, Auth, explicit grants, and RLS; WO-2026-09-19-supabase-opportunity-store.
QualifiesDEC-016, DEC-011, DEC-014
Revisit whenAuthenticated persistence creates unacceptable operational cost or security burden; the tracker is extracted into a standalone application with a different private store; or evidence shows canonical catalog authoring should move away from Git.
DEC-018AppliedTool-use and deployment boundary2026-09-21

Remote tool work batches evidence, CI, and review checkpoints

Separate repository validation from deployed-state verification: reuse still-valid remote evidence, batch coherent changes, use GitHub CI for repository correctness, and reserve Vercel Preview for materially user-reviewable or deployment-specific states.

QuestionHow should increasingly autonomous agents keep repository work safe and visible without making remote calls, commits, CI runs, and Vercel deployments scale with every internal iteration?
DecisionUse the Tool-use layer to require bounded evidence gathering, explicit freshness triggers, coherent batching, and cheapest-sufficient validation. GitHub is the default remote repository truth and CI validation surface; refresh it when evidence can materially change and immediately before consequential mutations. Vercel is the deployed-state verification surface: non-main intermediate commits are skipped by default, while agents deliberately create or allow a Preview for materially new user-reviewable states or questions that repository CI cannot answer. Keep Production deployment from main separate and consequential.
RationaleLive Vercel inspection for issue #159 found at least 20 Persona-Library deployments in roughly 35 minutes, including four errors, while no grouped production runtime errors were found in the inspected seven-day window. The commit sequence showed validation and diagnostic iterations repeatedly reaching deployment infrastructure. Reducing only Vercel builds would leave the broader remote-call pattern intact, while suppressing previews entirely would make work harder to steer.
AlternativesBuy more Vercel capacity; continue deploying every intermediate commit; disable previews entirely; or encode the behavior separately in every Persona and workflow. Rejected because these respectively mask the cause, preserve churn, reduce visibility, or duplicate vendor-specific execution guidance.
TradeoffsAgents must distinguish still-valid evidence from freshness-sensitive state and decide when a review checkpoint is materially useful. CI becomes a required repository validation layer, and Preview triggering gains a small amount of infrastructure logic. In return, remote cost and noise should fall without removing reviewability or safety.
AffectsTool discovery/safe execution guidance; GitHub and Vercel Tool-use recipes; Riley Tool requirements; repository AGENTS guidance; Work Order guidance; GitHub Actions validation; Vercel ignored-build configuration; issue #159.
EvidenceIssue #159; live Vercel deployment inspection on 2026-09-21; Persona-Library commit/deployment history; current Tool-use architecture and repository validation contracts.
Revisit whenRepresentative workstreams miss deployed defects, users receive review checkpoints too late to steer effectively, GitHub CI becomes materially more expensive than the avoided deployment churn, or Vercel/GitHub platform behavior changes the safe trigger model.
DEC-019AppliedRepository authorization boundary2026-09-21

Scoped implementation requests carry standing completion authorization

For Persona-Library, a scoped request to implement, fix, build, or complete repository work authorizes the normal implementation path through merge once current completion gates pass, unless the requester explicitly narrows the stopping boundary.

QuestionShould Persona-Library require a second user confirmation to merge after a requester has already asked it to implement scoped repository work and the current PR has passed review and validation?
DecisionTreat a scoped requester instruction to implement, fix, build, or complete Persona-Library work as standing completion authorization for branch/file changes, pull-request creation and updates, scoped review corrections, and merge into the default branch after fresh preflight. Explicit requester instructions such as do not merge, PR only, leave for review, or equivalent override the standing authorization. The standing rule is repository-specific and does not authorize unrelated issue mutation, repository settings/access changes, external repositories, external communications, or other out-of-scope consequential actions.
RationaleThe canonical GitHub Tool contract already allows merge when either the requester or repository contract authorizes it. Requiring an additional chat confirmation after every green implementation creates a redundant gate without adding new scope or safety. Safety comes from a clearly bounded initial request, independent review, required validation, fresh merge preflight, and explicit override handling—not from repeating the same approval after the work is complete.
AlternativesKeep a mandatory second merge confirmation; change the reusable GitHub Tool contract for every repository; infer merge permission from green CI alone; or auto-merge every open PR. Rejected because they respectively add redundant friction, broaden a Persona-Library-specific preference globally, confuse validation with authorization, or remove the scoped-request boundary.
TradeoffsAgents must preserve the exact original scope and requester overrides through the implementation lifecycle and must stop when current merge preflight exposes a blocker or out-of-scope side effect. In return, ordinary scoped implementation work can finish without an unnecessary conversational round trip while retaining fresh-state and review gates.
AffectsAGENTS.md; docs/playbooks/bounded-parallel-implementation.md; content/orientation/playbooks.json and generated mirror; docs/work-orders.md; focused governance validation; future Persona-Library Work Orders; issue #172.
EvidenceRequester direction on 2026-09-21; current rickvang/tool-repo GitHub contract revision 01198019e8f1520eb222dc6af2ec17bd81bc9c30; issue #172; prior issue #165/PR #166 consolidation of GitHub authorization semantics.
QualifiesDEC-010, DEC-018
Revisit whenStanding completion authorization causes unintended merges, requester overrides are not reliably preserved, repository review/validation gates materially change, or Persona-Library adopts a different default completion model.
DEC-020AppliedPrivate job-discovery state boundary2026-09-21

Authenticated storage becomes the durable seen-job set

Keep seen-job deduplication separate from Applications while moving repeated-search memory into a dedicated authenticated Supabase table in the existing private application-data project.

QuestionWhere should durable seen-job memory live now that repeated job-discovery runs need reliable suppression across sessions and authorized agent contexts, without turning Applications into a discovery-history ledger?
DecisionUse the existing authenticated persona-workspace-data Supabase project with a dedicated private app.seen_jobs table as the durable seen-job store. Persona-Library owns the reusable stable-identity behavior, browser storage adapter contract, database schema/migration, and validation; real seen-job rows remain private operational data outside Git. Read the owner-bound store before presenting results and insert only jobs actually presented afterward. Prefer provider/source plus stable provider job ID, then canonical source URL, then a conservative normalized company + title + location fingerprint. Do not silently fall back to local storage. Keep this store separate from app.opportunities, which remains the Applications lifecycle store.
RationaleThe earlier job-ledger boundary correctly kept private search history out of Git, but leaving the durable set only in a consuming runtime makes repeated searches unreliable across sessions and authorized agent contexts. DEC-017 already established authenticated Supabase with RLS as the private operational-state pattern for Applications. Reusing that project while creating a dedicated table preserves privacy and the separation between 'already shown' discovery memory and intentionally tracked opportunity lifecycle state.
AlternativesKeep the seen-job set only in caller memory or browser-local state; reuse app.opportunities; add seen/rejected/expired lifecycle fields to Applications; create a new Supabase project; or store seen-job history in Git. Rejected because they respectively fail durable cross-run suppression, conflate discovery with application lifecycle, expand the wrong state model, create unnecessary infrastructure, or violate the private-data boundary.
TradeoffsRepeated-search deduplication now depends on authenticated Supabase availability, RLS, and the existing private project. There is intentionally no silent local fallback, so an unavailable remote store must be surfaced rather than forking deduplication history. In return, the identity and privacy boundary is durable, testable, and reusable across authorized job-discovery runs.
Affectsclient/seen-job-store.js; dist/js/seen-job-store.js; docs/job-search/job-ledger-contract.md; docs/job-search/implementation.md; docs/work-orders/WO-2026-09-16-seen-job-dedup/database-contract.sql; repository validation; live app.seen_jobs schema/RLS; issue #96.
EvidenceIssue #96; PR #170; live persona-workspace-data migration create_app_seen_jobs; authenticated owner/cross-user RLS proof; repository validation for provider-ID precedence, URL canonicalization, conservative fallback identity, read-before-record behavior, repeated-run suppression, and no silent local fallback.
QualifiesDEC-011, DEC-017
Revisit whenThe seen-job store is extracted into a standalone job-search application with a different authenticated persistence layer; repeated-search behavior needs richer repost/version history; Supabase availability or security cost becomes unacceptable; or evidence shows discovery memory and application lifecycle should share a different explicitly designed state model.
DEC-021AppliedOrchestration state boundary2026-09-21

Riley resumes work from Current Work, then Work Orders, then live state

Use the existing Notion Current Work database as Riley's cross-agent workstream index, Work Orders as detailed execution/recovery state, and GitHub or other live systems as the authority for volatile operational facts.

QuestionHow should Riley preserve enough state for another agent to resume substantial work without duplicating fast-changing GitHub and tool state or reconstructing the entire conversation?
DecisionFor substantial Riley-operated work, create or resume one row in the user's existing Notion Current Work tracker when it is available. Keep that row concise and human-facing: objective, owner, next action, blocker, last checkpoint, and authoritative links. Use the linked Work Order for detailed scope, evidence, decisions, gates, handoffs, validation, and recovery. Treat GitHub, CI, reviews, mergeability, deployments, permissions, and other independently changing systems as freshness-sensitive authorities rather than mirrored tracker fields. Resume in the order Current Work → Work Order → selective live refresh, and update Current Work only at material lifecycle, ownership, blocker, or next-action transitions.
RationaleThe existing Current Work database was already designed as a cross-thread index and the Work Order already owns detailed resumable execution state. Creating another Riley database would duplicate state and create reconciliation overhead. Conversely, copying live repository facts into Notion would become stale and force additional verification. A clear state hierarchy preserves interruption recovery while allowing agents to reuse still-valid evidence and fetch only facts whose freshness matters.
AlternativesCreate a separate Riley orchestration database; make Work Orders the only cross-agent index; mirror full GitHub/CI state into Notion; or rely on each agent's conversation context. Rejected because they respectively duplicate the existing tracker, make portfolio-level resumption harder, create stale duplicated live state, or fail when a session or agent ends mid-work.
TradeoffsAgents must maintain concise Current Work checkpoints and correctly distinguish historical evidence from freshness-sensitive live state. Runtime enforcement still depends on agents loading the linked records. In return, substantial work can survive agent/session interruption with fewer broad rediscovery calls and less duplicated state.
AffectsRiley Morgan Persona and workflow; root AGENTS guidance; Work Order handoff/recovery contract; regression validation; Notion Current Work operating convention; issue #178.
EvidenceIssue #178; existing Notion Current Work purpose/schema observed on 2026-09-21; docs/work-orders.md recovery contract; issue #159 remote-tool efficiency lessons; Riley's existing AI-orchestrator responsibilities.
QualifiesDEC-018
Revisit whenCurrent Work becomes unavailable or is replaced; Work Orders no longer serve as detailed recovery packets; runtime orchestration gains a more reliable shared state service; or evidence shows the hierarchy causes stale decisions, duplicate work, or excessive tracker maintenance.
DEC-022AppliedOrchestration boundary2026-09-21

Riley governs durable orchestration for every substantial Current Work workstream

Make Riley Morgan / ai-orchestrator the default durable orchestration owner for substantial Current Work while preserving direct execution and the existing Current Work → Work Order → live-system hierarchy.

QuestionHow should Riley become a durable control plane across all substantial workstreams without forcing every execution step through an extra Riley runtime call or creating another orchestration database?
DecisionEvery substantial Current Work workstream is Riley-governed for continuity and orchestration unless the requester explicitly establishes another orchestration boundary. The selected Persona, Skill, Playbook, Tool path, or execution runtime may operate directly. Riley reconciles durable orchestration state at workstream creation, material rerouting, cross-agent handoff, major blocker, and completion. Current Work records Operating Route and optional Parent Work ID; Work Orders retain detailed recovery state; live systems retain volatile authority.
RationaleRiley already owns default intake/routing and cross-agent continuity. Extending that responsibility to every substantial Current Work item closes the remaining gap between initial routing and durable resumption without adding a second control database or a redundant execution hop.
TradeoffsAgents must load and honor the shared Riley invariant and maintain concise route state at material boundaries. The model deliberately does not prove that every runtime invoked Riley as a separate agent; it preserves orchestration ownership without adding that overhead.
AffectsRiley Morgan Persona and operating workflow; root AGENTS guidance; Work Order continuity contract; regression validation; Notion Current Work schema and governance; ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, and Hermes collaboration contracts; issue #180.
EvidenceIssue #180; Riley v1.4 continuity contract from issue #178; Notion Current Work Work ID, Operating Route, Parent Work ID, and Shared Collaboration Governance.
Revisit whenA user explicitly assigns another durable orchestration owner, direct execution becomes ambiguous or unsafe without a runtime Riley hop, or repeated work shows Operating Route / Parent Work ID are insufficient for resumption.
DEC-023AppliedOperational knowledge boundary2026-09-21

Operational knowledge stays attached to the capability that owns it

Make concrete good/bad execution examples first-class structured relationships on existing Skills and Tool-use recipes, with targeted retrieval and evidence lifecycle, instead of adding a generic knowledge-base space.

QuestionWhere should agents get concrete do/don't, call-order, freshness, stop, recovery, and good/bad examples so they stop reconstructing best practice on every run without creating another overlapping source of truth?
DecisionAdd structured Operational / Golden Scenario records as authored library data. Each scenario has one primary owning Skill or Tool-use recipe and may reference Personas or local Operating Pack context for routing. Normalize owner relationships and expose targeted matching so agents resolve the owner first and load only the smallest active scenario. Keep vendor-specific procedure in Tool-use recipes, project/domain rules in Operating Packs, and multi-stage coordination in Playbooks. Existing .golden.md files remain callable-Skill test fixtures rather than the canonical runtime knowledge store. Scenario evidence progresses conservatively from candidate to reviewed/validated guidance and never grants permission or overrides current source-of-truth rules.
RationaleThe current system already separates reusable judgment, Tool procedure, local context, and coordination. A new generic knowledge-base space would duplicate those owners and force agents to search a second taxonomy. At the same time, abstract guidance alone leaves too much execution shape to be reinvented. Relationship data closes that gap while preserving existing ownership and allowing targeted retrieval.
AlternativesCreate a new top-level Knowledge Base; make existing .golden.md test files the runtime source; put all examples directly into Skill practice; put every example into Tool-use recipes; or store all best practice in Operating Packs. Rejected because they respectively duplicate taxonomy, confuse tests with canonical knowledge, mix vendor execution into portable judgment, cannot cover non-Tool Skills, or turn project context into universal practice.
TradeoffsThe library gains another structured relationship type and agents must distinguish owner guidance from scenario examples and current live evidence. Scenario matching is intentionally lightweight rather than a semantic search service. In return, good execution becomes concrete and inspectable without another top-level space or broad context dump.
Affectscontent/library-data/operational-knowledge.js; content/library-model.js; Skills and Tool-use recipe relationships; Tool/Skill routing; root AGENTS guidance; docs/operational-knowledge.md; repository validation; generated library data; issue #185.
EvidenceIssue #185; existing Skill operation/quality guidance; DEC-018 remote-tool efficiency evidence; existing callable-Skill .golden.md fixtures; issue #182/#183 architecture Skill research and implementation.
QualifiesDEC-018, DEC-022
Revisit whenOperational Scenario volume, navigation, independent lifecycle, cross-owner reuse, or retrieval/index requirements can no longer be handled cleanly as relationships; or evidence shows agents routinely miss or misuse owner-scoped scenario retrieval.
DEC-024AppliedRepository operating boundary2026-09-23

Repository changes use a clean working copy, and Work Orders are recovery packets

Agents make Persona-Library file changes in a clean working copy created from freshly fetched origin/main, validate locally before pushing, and batch progress commits. Work Orders are created only when existing authoritative surfaces do not already preserve enough durable execution/recovery state.

QuestionHow can agents avoid the per-file API commits and CI-only feedback caused by the GitHub-only rule while keeping GitHub authoritative for remote state?
DecisionReplace the ban on local checkouts, worktrees, local edits, and local Git with a clean working copy on a task branch created from freshly fetched origin/main. Agents build and validate there with the CI commands and commit only the files the change owns. GitHub stays authoritative for issues, pull requests, reviews, checks, and mergeability, and required GitHub checks still gate merge. Define the small-change lane by execution/recovery-state footprint rather than semantic importance: omit a Work Order when Current Work plus the relevant issue/PR and domain-specific artifact already hold the durable state needed to resume and finish the work. One pull request or one session are useful heuristics, not gates; shared-schema, Decision, and governance changes may still qualify when their authoritative surfaces carry the plan, evidence boundary, and next action. Preserve existing issues, Current Work rows, WorkNodes, and domain records such as Test Queue when they have their own lifecycle; do not create duplicate trackers merely because the Work Order is omitted. Create a Work Order when interrupted, cross-agent, multi-phase, gate-heavy, or otherwise complex work needs unique resumable state.
RationaleThe GitHub-only rule from #104 prevented stale local state but forced agents to change files one API call at a time and to learn about failures only from CI. At d93a4c7, PR #200 had 50 single-file commits and 30 CI runs on its branch, PR #198 had 26 commits, PR #184 had 21, and main carries 10 hand-applied "Generate Applications navigation" commits. CI itself is fast (median 13 s across the 25 most recent runs), so the cost is agent turns and round trips. A working copy created from freshly fetched origin/main keeps the freshness protection without that cost, and the pinned GitHub Tool contract already treats local files as authoritative only for the checked-out tree. The TQ-40-001 / #205 correction on 2026-09-23 showed the same duplication problem at the orchestration layer: deferred verification already had an issue, Current Work pointer, source implementation, and Test Queue record, yet a new Work Order duplicated that state and accidentally kept Current Work open. The recovery-state criterion removes that coupling without discarding Work Orders where they add unique value.
AlternativesKeep the ban and batch commits through the Git Data API; allow any existing checkout; require Work Orders for every non-trivial or shared-schema change; drop Work Orders entirely; or change the reusable GitHub Tool contract. Rejected because they respectively still prevent local builds and validation, reintroduce stale-state risk, create duplicate lifecycle state, lose recovery state for genuinely interruptible multi-agent work, or broaden a Persona-Library choice to every repository.
TradeoffsAgents must fetch before branching, rebase and re-validate when main moves, and avoid committing unrelated generated or local files. They must also judge whether existing authoritative surfaces are sufficient for recovery; under-documenting complex handoffs is a risk, while overusing Work Orders recreates duplicate state. The contract therefore makes recovery-state sufficiency the gate and keeps required GitHub checks, impact reconciliation, domain records, and Work Graph obligations independent of Work Order presence.
AffectsAGENTS.md rules 10–12; ARCHITECTURE.md; docs/work-orders.md; docs/work-orders/README.md and archive README; content/orientation/docs.json and generated mirror; UX active-work guidance; Work Graph orchestration guidance; GitHub issue-implementation Operational Scenario and generated library data; repository validation; Current Work / Test Queue boundary; issues #203 and #205.
EvidenceIssue #203; commit counts on PRs #200, #198, and #184; the 25 most recent CI run durations on 2026-09-23; rickvang/tool-repo tools/github/ACCESS.md section 4 at 01198019e8f1520eb222dc6af2ec17bd81bc9c30; issue #196 first-pass audit; issue #205 and TQ-40-001 lifecycle correction on 2026-09-23
QualifiesDEC-018, DEC-021, DEC-022
Revisit whenWorking copies cause stale-state merges or unrelated files in commits; local and CI validation diverge; agents cannot reliably decide when existing surfaces provide sufficient recovery state; work repeatedly becomes unresumable without a Work Order; duplicate Work Orders continue to mirror issue/Current Work/Test Queue state; or commits per pull request and task time do not fall.
